title: The Nets Begin to Break
text:
In the Gospel of Luke, Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret, with a crowd pressing in to hear him. He saw two boats at the shore, where the fishermen had stepped out and were washing their nets. He got into one, which belonged to Simon, and asked him to push out a little from the land. Then he sat down and taught the crowd from the boat.

When he finished speaking, he told Simon to put out into deep water and let down the nets for a catch. Simon answered that they had worked hard all night and caught nothing. But because Jesus said so, he would let down the nets.

They did, and they caught such a great number of fish that their nets began to break. So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them. The partners came, and they filled both boats so full that the boats began to sink.

Simon fell at Jesus' knees, overwhelmed, and so were his partners, James and John, the sons of Zebedee. Jesus told Simon not to be afraid: from now on he would be catching people. And when they brought their boats to land, they left everything and followed him.
lesson: When a success is too big for you to handle alone, call your partners right away rather than letting the nets break. Good fortune also needs a team.
location: Lake of Gennesaret (Sea of Galilee, modern Israel)
